provenance: FIXTURE, not user evidence. The corpus mixes products and formats, as a real library does. Eight short texts are the library documents scripts/seed_demo.py publishes (titles ending in '(sample)'), kept word for word. Six files under library/ (titles ending in '(fixture)') are written by scripts/build_library_golden_corpus.py, one product and one format each: a Word guide with headings and a table, a two-page PDF, a slide deck with a table, a spreadsheet rate card, a CSV procedure, and a long Markdown policy whose paragraphs the chunker splits. Every case and expected passage was written by hand from these documents, not from historic requirements or from knowledge admins' searches. An expected passage is a piece of the document's wording, wherever the extractor puts it; an expected document with no passage means any of its passages answers. Cases marked 'semantic' share few words with their passage: the fake hash embedding may miss them, and they are there to be measured against real embeddings.
